transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-13
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Oliver Hayes (CTO - Stonegate), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Nora Fields (Security PM)
Shared links: onboarding-runbook-v3.pdf, security-pack-v2.docx, benchmark-sample-payloads.xlsx

[00:00] Maya: ok welcome everyone thanks for making time for the kickoff, I think we'll keep this tight 45-60 mins, run through scope, network and security, and then a quick timeline. Hey Oliver good to see you.
[00:18] Oliver: yeah thanks Maya appreciate it. Busy week but um excited to get this rolling.
[00:32] Maya: quick intros just so names line up, I'm Maya Patel AE at Redwood, with me Ethan Cole SE and Priya our CSM. From Stonegate?
[00:40] Oliver: Oliver Hayes CTO, Lena Ortiz Head of ML, Samir Khan Platform engineering, Nora Fields sec PM.
[00:47] Maya: awesome, cool. I'll kick off with proposed pilot goals — this is not a full prod rollout, it's a sprint to validate latency and integration with your berth line (means backline?), and to exercise our Dedicated/Private options for data residency. 
[01:05] Lena: yeah the two things for us are: 1) that the model responses meet business quality for our customer-facing summaries, 2) that we can host in a VPC that meets our SOC2 controls.
[01:17] Maya: great. Ethan will you walk through the tech sketch and the benchmark plan?
[01:22] Ethan: sure. So at a high level - Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, or private VPC/on-prem - for the pilot we suggested dedicated capacity in a single region to get predictable latency. We'll test using your sample payloads — low latency prompts (single-turn) and longer multi-turn chat. The goal is look at p95 latency and token cost per session.
[01:46] Samir: question — for dedicated pools, how does network egress work? We have strict egress rules and need to route through our NAT gateway and use private peering. 
[01:56] Ethan: good q. For Dedicated we can support VPC peering and private routing. There are two patterns: a private control plane with data paths over peering or the on-prem package that keeps everything in your network. We'll follow up with a network diagram template but technically yes, you can keep egress limited.
[02:18] Nora: also KMS: we need to ensure encryption at rest with our key. Do you integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:25] Maya: yes we do. We support KMS integrations for Private deployments, and customer-managed keys for Dedicated in many configurations. We'll send the security pack that details supported cloud KMS providers and HSM options.
[02:40] Oliver: perfect, that matters. On data retention, we want ephemeral storage by default and a 30-day audit log. Is that something Redwood supports out of box?
[02:50] Priya: we typically default to no retention for hosted, and Dedicated/Private can be configured to your retention policy. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll map that in the runbook.
[03:05] Lena: for the quality story — we need to run automated evals on 5k prompts and see regression windows. Do you have a suggested harness?
[03:14] Ethan: yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval templates but for pilot we'll provide a simple eval harness and sample scripts. We'll also snapshot model versions so you can reproduce results.
[03:28] Samir: anything about tokenization differences? We have language clients in both Python and Golang.
[03:34] Ethan: SDKs in Python/Node officially, but REST works fine with Go. Tokenization differences usually show up in cost estimates; we'll include tokenization notes in the benchmark plan.
[03:46] Oliver: timeline — we're aiming for an internal demo in 4 weeks if possible. Can Redwood commit to helping get us there?
[03:53] Maya: yes that's feasible. Proposed plan: week 0 (this week) align on scope and network/security; week 1 Redwood delivers runbook and SE benchmark plan and we ingest your sample data; week 2 perform bench tests and iterate; week 3 integrate end-to-end and validation; week 4 internal demo.
[04:12] Nora: that sounds ambitious but OK. We'll need to check calendar for the infra walkthrough.
[04:20] Maya: noted. I'll add the on-prem/infrastructure walkthrough as a required step — SE and your infra team meet for 60–90 minutes.
[04:29] Lena: who should be in that meeting from Redwood?
[04:32] Priya: Ethan plus a runtime engineer ideally. I'll coordinate.
[04:37] Ethan: yep I can bring runtime. Also quick note on cost controls — we recommend a small dedicated pool with autoscaling and token caps so you don't get surprised.
[04:48] Samir: cool. About SSO — we want RBAC integration via SAML and SCIM provisioning, is that part of the onboarding?
[04:56] Maya: yes SSO/SAML and SCIM are standard enterprise features, we'll include SAML metadata exchange in the security packet.
[05:05] Oliver: ok great. Any blockers we foresee?
[05:08] Ethan: a couple: 1) network peering details can add latency if not configured correctly, 2) pilot data extraction — we need sanitized subset or synthetic data for the initial run, 3) if you need air-gapped on-prem we need to align on ordering for the package.
[05:27] Nora: on air-gap — not this phase, we just need strict VPC controls.
[05:31] Maya: good. Let's talk specifics of the benchmark — p95, p99 latencies and token cost, and also golden evaluation metrics on your 5k prompt set. Ethan, you want to share the sample benchmark matrix?
[05:44] Ethan: yes — we'll measure cold start, steady-state throughput, per-token CPU/GPU usage, cache hit rates on prefixes, and an accuracy pass. We'll post numbers into the shared spreadsheet.
[05:58] Lena: what's the expected p95 for a 2k token prompt on a dedicated A100-like pool? Rough estimate.
[06:06] Ethan: ballpark — depends on model and quantization; for an Llama2-ish 13B variant optimized on A100 we typically see p95 in the 200-450ms range for shorter prompts; 2k tokens can push multiple seconds, but we can give a concrete baseline after the bench.
[06:26] Oliver: understood. Also curious about fallback policies if capacity spikes. How do rollbacks/automatic fallbacks work?
[06:33] Maya: Redwood has routing policies — you can set automatic fallback to a cheaper variant or hosted mode. For pilot we'll propose a soft-fail strategy and alerting to avoid customer-facing errors.
[06:45] Samir: logging and observability, can we get token-level breakdowns per request? We need to tie costs back to feature owners.
[06:53] Priya: yes that's part of Redwood Console — token/time breakdown, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks we can enable for the pilot.
[07:05] Nora: security question — do you support customer audit log exports to our Splunk/GCP logging?
[07:10] Ethan: yes log export to S3/GCS and direct streaming to SIEM are supported. We'll include example configs.
[07:18] Maya: quick check — anyone here on the call who will be the main point of contact for day-to-day?
[07:23] Oliver: Samir will be primary for infra, Lena for ML, Nora for security, and I'll be the exec sponsor.
[07:30] Maya: perfect. 
[07:34] (brief crosstalk) 
[07:36] Maya: ok last bit — success criteria for pilot: 1) p95 latency within target and consistent over 3 days, 2) generated output passes automated eval with <5% regression vs baseline, 3) security checklist completed and KMS integrated. Are we aligned?
[07:53] Lena: yes that's good.
[07:55] Oliver: yes.
[07:56] Maya: great. I'll recap actions and owners.
[08:00] Maya: Action recap: Redwood sends onboarding runbook and security packet (Maya), SE runs bench plan and shares artifacts (Ethan), Stonegate provides sample prompts and retention policy (Oliver/Nora), schedule infra walkthrough (Priya).
[08:18] Nora: quick follow up — on the security questionnaire, are you expecting network configs from us or will you provide templates?
[08:25] Priya: we'll send a network diagram template and a checklist; if you can fill the network bits we can draft peering steps.
[08:33] Samir: one more, about model versions — can we pin a model and still allow auto-updates? we want reproducibility.
[08:40] Ethan: yes you can pin model versions for the pilot, and we support controlled rollouts if you want to test new versions behind canary.
[08:49] Oliver: ok sounds good. Anything else?
[08:52] (silence)
[08:54] Maya: that's all from us. We'll send notes and the packet by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
[09:02] Lena: thanks, bye.
[09:04] Oliver: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcript quality: some speaker labels were manual, pockets of audio overlap; proper nouns sometimes mis-transcribed (e.g., model names). The recording length matches the stated duration approximately.
